correctness.rationale: The stated normalized windows give squared radial ambiguity multipliers e^(−s) and e^(−s)L(s)^2. The factorization L²−1=s(s−4)(s−2)²/4 forces the Gaussian optimum before 4 except at T=2, where the pointwise inequalities give the exact interval [0,η]. With u=2−s the threshold function is 4∫_0^1 e^(−tu)dt/[u(2−u)(2+u)]; its log is strictly convex in 0<u<2, so the interior minimizer can be found by a single stationarity equation. At s=4 all weights agree. The derivative there is e^(−4)(4w−1), and the w=1/4 derivative factorization proves the plateau and specifies its exit on the descending branch. This gives the whole optimizer interval at T=4 and strict uniqueness on 4<T≤T_*. Thereafter reflection about s=2 and the monotonicity of D on (2+√2,4) locate the inner minimum. The outer interval has endpoint minimum, so the strictly decreasing inner envelope and increasing outer endpoint as functions of w cross exactly once. For every s≥T_*>8, D(s)≤D(8)=−84, so F_w(T) strictly decreases in T for all w and the crossing moves strictly to the right. Near w=1 the inner active radius differs from 2+√2 by O(1−w); hence the inner envelope has leading term e^(−2−√2)(1−w), which proves both large-T limits. Independent bounded reproduction yields η=0.745182361841, T_*=8.83273551863978 and, at T=10, w=0.388201417353 and Γ=0.016964744328.
